title: Rethinking Efficient Crack Segmentation with Task-Aligned Structural-Directional Modeling (RIFT)
mechanism: Treats crack segmentation as sparse structural recovery: local-evidence blocks, large directional strip kernels that aggregate continuity along orientations, and a light multi-scale decoder; 0.47 to 1.69 M parameters.
adaptation: (a) Benchmark row: RIFT-B on crack + inactive + background, 1-channel stem, 512 px, BCE-Dice. (b) Model arm: fuse RIFT crack logits with the house model (heterogeneous ensemble) or graft the directional block as a crack branch at strides 1-2 of the U-Net++ decoder. Check strip kernels against busbars and fingers, which are long straight lines.
min_experiment: Arm A RIFT-B alone; arm B PF + RIFT crack logit average; baselines PF single and PF 2-seed ensemble; 3 seeds. Metric: CV crack IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill arm B if it does not beat the 2-seed PF ensemble by +0.01 CV crack IoU or +0.03 E1 relF1@2; keep arm A as a benchmark row.
evidence: R: best or tied-best on 16 metrics across DeepCrack, CamCrack789, CrackMap, Crack500 (3 seeds); cross-dataset average 2-class mIoU 77.0 vs SCSegamba 74.6 and MixerCSeg 71.0; clDice 90.6.
prior_overlap: none. No crack-specific architecture or heterogeneous ensemble has been run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark baseline with a 24-class head. Its directional-continuity block is a candidate drop-in for the U-Net++ decoder. Its protocol (reproduced baselines plus topology-aware evaluation) is a template for the EL benchmark.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark row vs house, 3 seeds. Block-in-house arm: kill if crack relF1@2 and components found both gain < 0.012.
